description: Fork of exp268 (hybrid E=64 b=8 -> 1.6351) with device_batch_size 8 -> 32. Same change pattern as exp267 (b=32 over exp265 b=8 -> 1.4504). Tests whether the dense-Adam-stats benefit of bigger batches at E=96 also holds at E=64, where the residual stream is 33% smaller but qk/v capacity (d_qk=64, d_v=32) is preserved. Memory estimate: ~30-35 GB peak on 80 GB H100 (smaller than exp267's ~42 GB because residual is smaller). Comparators: exp267=1.4504 (E=96 hybrid b=32), exp268=1.6351 (E=64 hybrid b=8). Hypothesis: if E=64 mostly preserves capacity, exp269 lands ~1.47-1.49 with ~30% fewer params than exp267 — would be an extremely compact LUT-LM SOTA candidate.
